If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence in upward bias.

If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending up, cap the 7–14 day forecast at +1.5% above recent peak to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33–0.67) and forecast is below true path, add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for mid-horizon (8–21 days) to align with sentiment momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for late horizon (22–30 days) to reflect bearish sentiment decay.

If sentiment is positive and true path is trending down, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid-horizon to avoid sentiment-driven overoptimism.

If forecast is above true path by >1.5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for late horizon to correct for overfitting sentiment signals.
